description: Request-side contracts every case invoke/query action must meet before it reaches the product (step2r round 12, run-driven: docs/execution/s5a-adapter/run-61bd0f8a.json showed every api command and most queries rejected for envelope shape). verification/cases/request_contract.py applies and checks them; ./verify prepare runs verification/cases/check_request_contracts.py (PreparationAssetChecks 'request-contracts'), so a violation fails preparation and a recorded product gap prints KNOWN_OPEN. Step 2 round 13 replaces grantComposition with grantAuthorization: one all-of grant per actor, checked statically against every authorized read and command and every pinned FORBIDDEN. Product code is read, never changed.

commandRoutes.provenanceRule: provenance names every slot exactly once. A value whose provenance the case states (formerly embedded in the slot value or a per-slot valueProvenance map) keeps it. Otherwise a value the requester picked from the fixture world or an earlier response ($alias, $result, $transform, typed {type,id} or a list of only those) is CONTEXT, and a literal the requester typed in the request (text, decimal, boolean, quantity, aggregate) is USER. APPROVED_DEFAULT is never inferred; only a case statement sets it. A blanket valueProvenance string is not a per-slot statement and is ignored.

harnessDeclarations.mcp: MCP protocol fields outside tool arguments: transport rpcId, MRTR requestState and inputResponses (V6)
harnessDeclarations.intentionalViolation: a field the case sends on purpose to prove the product rejects it; prepare requires the declared fields to equal the actual violations and a pinned rejection on the action

grantAuthorization.rule: User decision 2026-10-09 (AGENTS.md): a grant naming several dimension kinds authorizes only when every kind matches the targets the product presents (all-of, IdentityAuthorization.permittedScopes); identifiers within one kind are alternatives, and the policy guard requires every presented identifier of a command (PolicyCommandGuard.everyScope). The fixture schema and the Step 3 installer hold one grant per actor, so a fixture grant keeps only the dimension kinds that every capability the cases call with that actor presents (directly or through it as a fixture delegator): ITEM when all those capabilities carry the item (familiesWithoutItem name those that do not), none otherwise (an organization-wide grant). WORK, PLACE, TARGET and SOURCE restrictions of a multi-purpose grant would refuse its own reads (an inventory or item row presents no WORK; a Work presents no PLACE), so conform_fixture drops them unless an override keeps them for a negative oracle. Keys with no product grant scope kind are dropped too: the installer could not install them. check_request_contracts.py then proves statically, per subcase, that every read or command the case expects to be authorized is covered and that every action pinned to FORBIDDEN stays uncovered.

commandSlots.description: Slots each command capability declares (step2r round 13, item 2 and 3 of docs/execution/step2r-round13/README.md). The plan names the inputs of each command (sections 5.2 and 6) but not their slot names; the published Step 3 capability contracts (docs/execution/s2-inventory/contracts.md for the stock commands, docs/execution/s4-sales/contracts.md for delivery) and, where no contract document exists, the handler allowlists transcribed here name them. Each entry cites its source. allowed: the slots the handler accepts (a handler without an allowlist ignores others, which is noted). required: the slots it rejects a command without (TYPE_INVALID before authorization).

declaredOnlyCases.reason: These cases send one shared slot set to every capability, so the product rejected them with TYPE_INVALID before the authorization they test (run-85ce2365 and probe-85ce2365: expected FORBIDDEN observed TYPE_INVALID; V7 sends the same set to its dispatches). conform_intent projects each command onto its declared slots: a declared slot takes its value from the same slot, a listed rename, the typed subject, the request evidenceRefs or the product clock; undeclared slots are dropped. Deliberate violations stay (action.harness.intentionalViolation).

knownOpen.reason: A command omits a slot its capability requires, so the product answers TYPE_INVALID before authorization and before the business rule the case tests.
